subject: Reasoning
topic: Puzzles Mixed II — Linear Row, Box Stacking, Floor and Circular Arrangement (W13 B1)

questions.stem: Five people P, Q, R, S and T sit in a single row. R sits at the extreme left. S sits immediately to the right of R. T sits at the extreme right. P sits at the 3rd position from the left. Who sits 3rd from the right?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Build the arrangement: R at 1, S immediately right of R → S at 2. T at 5 (extreme right). P at 3. Remaining: Q at 4. Arrangement: R(1)–S(2)–P(3)–Q(4)–T(5). 3rd from right in a 5-person row: position = 5−3+1 = 3. Position 3 = P. Verify: from right: T(1st), Q(2nd), P(3rd) ✓.

questions.stem: Using the arrangement from the previous question [R–S–P–Q–T], how many people sit between S and Q?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Arrangement: R(1)–S(2)–P(3)–Q(4)–T(5). S is at position 2, Q is at position 4. People between positions 2 and 4: only position 3 = P. Count = 1.

questions.stem: Five boxes A, B, C, D and E are stacked one on top of another. A is at the bottom. C is immediately above B. D is immediately above C. B is immediately above A. E is at the top. Which box is in the 3rd position from the bottom?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Build from clues: A at bottom (1). B immediately above A → B at 2. C immediately above B → C at 3. D immediately above C → D at 4. E at top (5). Stack: A(1)–B(2)–C(3)–D(4)–E(5). 3rd from bottom = C ✓.

questions.stem: Using the stack arrangement [A–B–C–D–E from bottom to top], how many boxes are above C and below E?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Stack: A(1)–B(2)–C(3)–D(4)–E(5). Above C (position 3) and below E (position 5): only position 4 = D. Count = 1.

questions.stem: Six people A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a row. A sits at the extreme left. D is immediately right of A. B sits 3rd from the left. C sits immediately right of B. F sits at the extreme right. E sits between C and F. Who is 4th from the right?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Build from clues: A at 1. D immediately right of A → D at 2. B at 3. C immediately right of B → C at 4. F at 6. E between C(4) and F(6) → E at 5. Arrangement: A(1)–D(2)–B(3)–C(4)–E(5)–F(6). 4th from right = 6−4+1 = 3rd from left? No: 4th from right means: from right — F(1st), E(2nd), C(3rd), B(4th). 4th from right = B ✓.

questions.stem: Using the 6-person row arrangement [A–D–B–C–E–F], how many people sit to the right of D?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Arrangement: A(1)–D(2)–B(3)–C(4)–E(5)–F(6). D is at position 2. People to the right of D: positions 3, 4, 5, 6 = B, C, E, F. Count = 4.

questions.stem: Five athletes P, Q, R, S and T finished a race. T finished before R. R finished before S. P finished last. Q finished immediately before P. Who finished 3rd?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Chain: T before R before S. P is last (5th). Q immediately before P → Q at 4th, P at 5th. T, R, S fill positions 1, 2, 3 in that order: T(1st)–R(2nd)–S(3rd)–Q(4th)–P(5th). Verify: T before R ✓; R before S ✓; Q immediately before P ✓; P last ✓. 3rd = S.

questions.stem: Six people live on six different floors (Floor 1 = lowest, Floor 6 = top). B lives on the top floor. D lives on the bottom floor. A lives on Floor 3. C lives immediately above A. E lives between C and B. F lives between D and A. Who lives on Floor 2?
questions.explanation: C is correct. B at 6, D at 1, A at 3. C immediately above A → C at 4. E between C(4) and B(6) → E at 5. F between D(1) and A(3) → F at 2. Floor arrangement: D(1)–F(2)–A(3)–C(4)–E(5)–B(6). Floor 2 = F ✓.

questions.stem: Using the floor arrangement [D–F–A–C–E–B from bottom to top], how many people live above C?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Floor arrangement: D(1)–F(2)–A(3)–C(4)–E(5)–B(6). C is on Floor 4. People above C: Floor 5 = E and Floor 6 = B. Count = 2.

questions.stem: Six people A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table facing the centre. E sits immediately to the right of A. B sits 2nd to the right of A. C sits immediately to the right of B. D sits immediately to the left of A. F sits between C and D (going clockwise from C). Who sits directly opposite A?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Fix A at position 1 (clockwise: 1→2→3→4→5→6→1). E immediately right of A → E at 2. B 2nd right of A → B at 3. C immediately right of B → C at 4. D immediately left of A: left of position 1 (anticlockwise) = position 6 → D at 6. F between C(4) and D(6) going clockwise → F at 5. Circle: A(1)–E(2)–B(3)–C(4)–F(5)–D(6). Directly opposite A in a 6-person circle: position 1 + 3 = position 4 = C ✓. Trap: students may incorrectly calculate opposite as 'immediate left or right' rather than 3 positions away in a 6-person circle.
